title: Muxed address from the largest uint64 ID, 2^64-1, encodes exactly
why: 2^64-1 is the largest valid muxed ID; it exceeds int64 and float precision, so a builder that routes it through a signed or floating type changes it.
notes: Built by xdrcheck-corpus synth from corpus/recipes/cap-0027/api-muxed-account-id-encoding.id-2-pow-64-minus-1.json. Origin: probe vector 2m2, in evidence/sdk-matrix/vectors/vectors.json, executed in every probe column (evidence/sdk-matrix). The M-address is the SEP-0023 encoding of key || ffffffffffffffff (the SEP-0023 muxed test vector form); the XDR is KEY_TYPE_MUXED_ED25519, the id, the key. The ID is passed as a decimal string, the form the JavaScript SDK's MuxedAccount takes (from 17.3.0 it refuses any other type); the Python SDK takes only an integer and refuses the string, a typing refusal rather than a defect. Expected values were computed from the XDR definitions, the CAP or SEP text and the stellar-core rule cited under related, with an independent encoder; no SDK output was used.
